immutable_state.instructions: Does the supplied production code keep domain state transitions non-mutating and protect domain values across ownership boundaries?

criteria.pass: Domain transitions preserve caller-owned inputs and previously published snapshots by returning new values rather than mutating them in place, and values crossing ownership boundaries are immutable, defensively copied, or governed by a clear non-mutating ownership contract. Freshly allocated or cloned local scratch objects and collections built and returned without aliasing caller-owned inputs, per-call accumulators and parsing loops, UI or framework lifecycle, cancellation, or sequence coordination handles/refs, stateless or read-only view components and adapters that forward callbacks without mutating domain state, SDK/client infrastructure handles, persistence/storage effects, and intentionally scoped infrastructure caches all pass cleanly. Absence of language-level immutability annotations (such as read-only or final field modifiers) alone does not fail when values are not mutated across boundaries.
criteria.fail: A domain transition mutates caller-owned or previously published domain objects or collections in place, exposes internal mutable structures across an ownership boundary where callers can corrupt domain state, or stores unisolated mutable domain state shared across independent callers or runs. Do NOT fail freshly allocated or cloned local scratch objects/collections populated and returned without mutating caller-owned inputs, UI/framework lifecycle, cancellation, or sequence coordination handles/refs, or stateless/read-only view components and adapters that forward callbacks without mutating domain state.

domain_invariants.instructions: Do the domain types or domain construction functions in the supplied production code own and enforce their intrinsic invariants?

criteria.pass: Domain concepts with validity rules, constrained sets of states, or domain behavior use dedicated domain types, enums/unions, or validated constructors/factories that enforce their intrinsic invariants (pure enums/unions or value types with no extra validity constraints also pass). Dedicated boundary, parser, formatter, UI, or entry-point code passes when it delegates domain construction or validation to those domain types or factories.
criteria.fail: Core logic represents structured domain concepts or constrained states with raw unvalidated primitives, magic strings/numbers, or untyped pairs/tuples, or enforces domain invariants only ad hoc in parsers/callers/views while leaving domain creation able to produce invalid states.

boundary_separation.instructions: Does the supplied production code keep transport/UI concerns (external I/O, input parsing, output formatting/rendering, and protocol error mapping) and storage mechanics cleanly separated from core domain and application logic?

criteria.pass: External I/O, input parsing, output formatting or UI rendering, and transport error mapping (such as HTTP status codes or protocol exceptions) are isolated at the entry-point or UI boundary, and storage mechanics (such as queries, transactions, optimistic-concurrency/CAS persistence guards, row mapping, or browser-storage serialization) stay in persistence code. Core domain and application logic operates strictly on typed domain values and domain outcomes without reading files or streams, parsing raw external text, formatting protocol output, or throwing transport-specific exceptions.
criteria.fail: Core domain, application, or persistence code directly handles transport or UI concerns (such as parsing raw external text/tokens, formatting protocol output, or throwing HTTP/transport status exceptions), OR transport/UI handlers or persistence adapters embed core business rules and workflow coordination instead of keeping them separate.
